units.t: Old English and the Epic: Beowulf

learn: Anglo-Saxon tribes settled in England from the 400s, bringing Old English and a warrior culture.
Values included loyalty to a lord, courage, generosity and fame after death.
Scops (poets) performed poems from memory in mead halls.
lessons.try: Compare Anglo-Saxon heroic values with those of a modern hero.

learn: "Beowulf" (written down around 1000) tells how Beowulf defeats Grendel, Grendel's mother and a dragon.
It mixes pagan heroic values with Christian ideas.
Beowulf's final battle reflects on mortality and leadership.
check: The poem mixes heroic and ___ ideas.
lessons.try: Trace how Beowulf changes from young warrior to old king.

learn: Old English poetry uses alliteration and a caesura (pause) in each line.
Kennings are compound metaphors: "whale-road" for the sea.
Translations, such as Francis Gummere's (1910, public domain), keep these features.
lessons.try: Invent five kennings for everyday objects.

lessons.t: The Norman Conquest and Middle English
learn: The Norman Conquest (1066) brought French into English.
Middle English (about 1100-1500) blended Old English and French.
Many English words for food and law come from French.
check: Middle English blended Old English and...
lessons.try: List ten English words with French origins.

learn: Geoffrey Chaucer's "The Canterbury Tales" (late 1300s) follows pilgrims telling stories.
The General Prologue describes characters from every level of society.
Chaucer uses satire to criticise corrupt church officials.
lessons.try: Write a General Prologue-style portrait of a modern character.

learn: A frame story holds many stories inside one.
"The Wife of Bath's Tale" asks what women most desire.
"Sir Gawain and the Green Knight" is a romance about honour and temptation.
check: The Wife of Bath asks what women...
lessons.try: Analyse how Gawain's test reveals his character.

learn: "Macbeth" (about 1606) was written under King James I, who was interested in witchcraft.
Macbeth is a brave general who murders King Duncan after the witches' prophecy.
Lady Macbeth pushes him toward the crime.
check: The play was written under King...
lessons.try: Chart how the witches' prophecies shape Macbeth's choices.

learn: Unchecked ambition leads Macbeth from crime to tyranny.
Guilt appears as visions: the dagger, Banquo's ghost, Lady Macbeth's sleepwalking.
"Out, damned spot!" shows guilt Lady Macbeth cannot wash away.
lessons.try: Analyse the sleepwalking scene.

learn: Tragedy follows a hero's fall caused by a flaw.
"Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow" reflects despair at life's meaninglessness.
Imagery of blood, darkness and sleep runs through the play.
check: An image pattern in Macbeth is...
lessons.try: Track one image pattern through the play.

learn: Petrarchan sonnets have an octave and sestet; Shakespearean sonnets have three quatrains and a couplet.
Shakespeare's Sonnet 18 begins "Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?"
The volta is the turn in thought.
check: A Shakespearean sonnet ends with a...
lessons.try: Write a Shakespearean sonnet.

learn: John Donne used conceits (extended, surprising metaphors).
"A Valediction: Forbidding Mourning" compares lovers to a compass.
Andrew Marvell's "To His Coy Mistress" argues "seize the day".
lessons.try: Explain the compass conceit.

learn: John Milton's "Paradise Lost" (1667) retells the Fall in blank verse.
Satan is a complex, persuasive figure.
Milton wrote it after going blind.
check: Milton was ___ when he wrote it.
lessons.try: Analyse Satan's speech "Better to reign in Hell".

learn: The Enlightenment (late 1600s-1700s) valued reason, science and order.
Writers used wit and satire to expose foolishness.
Alexander Pope used heroic couplets.
lessons.try: Write a heroic couplet about school life.

learn: "Gulliver's Travels" (1726) satirises politics and human nature.
"A Modest Proposal" (1729) shocks readers to expose the cruel treatment of the Irish poor.
Irony means saying the opposite of what is meant.
lessons.try: Explain the irony in "A Modest Proposal".

learn: Daniel Defoe's "Robinson Crusoe" (1719) is an early English novel.
Samuel Johnson's Dictionary (1755) standardised English.
Mary Wollstonecraft's "A Vindication of the Rights of Woman" (1792) argued for women's education.
lessons.try: Summarise Wollstonecraft's argument.

learn: William Wordsworth and Samuel Taylor Coleridge published "Lyrical Ballads" (1798).
Wordsworth described poetry as "the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings".
Romantics valued nature, imagination and ordinary language.
check: "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner" is by...
lessons.try: Write a poem about a place in nature you remember.

learn: Byron, Shelley and Keats wrote passionate, rebellious poetry.
Shelley's "Ozymandias" shows the fall of a proud king.
Keats's odes explore beauty and mortality: "Beauty is truth, truth beauty".
lessons.try: Analyse irony in "Ozymandias".

learn: Mary Shelley's "Frankenstein" (1818) explores ambition, creation and responsibility.
The creature is rejected and becomes violent.
It is often called the first science fiction novel.
check: It is often called the first ___ novel.
lessons.try: Debate who is the real monster in "Frankenstein".

learn: Queen Victoria reigned 1837-1901, during the Industrial Revolution and empire.
Writers examined poverty, class and morality.
Literacy and serialised novels grew.
lessons.try: Research one social problem of Victorian England.

learn: Charles Dickens's "Great Expectations" (1861) follows Pip's rise and moral growth.
Charlotte Brontë's "Jane Eyre" (1847) tells of an independent woman.
Thomas Hardy showed fate and rural change.
lessons.try: Compare how Pip and Jane seek identity.

learn: Tennyson's "Ulysses" urges "to strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield".
Robert Browning perfected the dramatic monologue ("My Last Duchess").
Elizabeth Barrett Browning wrote "How Do I Love Thee?"
check: "How Do I Love Thee?" is by...
lessons.try: Analyse what the Duke reveals in "My Last Duchess".

learn: Wilfred Owen's "Dulce et Decorum Est" (written 1917) shows the horror of a gas attack.
Owen calls the old saying "the old Lie".
War poetry rejected glorified images of battle.
check: War poets rejected ___ images of battle.
lessons.try: Analyse the imagery in "Dulce et Decorum Est".

learn: James Joyce and Virginia Woolf used stream of consciousness.
Woolf's "A Room of One's Own" (1929) argues women need money and space to write.
Joseph Conrad's "Heart of Darkness" (1899) questions imperialism.
check: Woolf argued women need money and a...
lessons.try: Write a stream-of-consciousness paragraph.

learn: George Orwell's "Animal Farm" and "1984" warn against totalitarianism.
Postcolonial writers such as Chinua Achebe ("Things Fall Apart", 1958) answered colonial stories.
Literature in English became global.
lessons.try: Compare Conrad's and Achebe's views of Africa.

learn: College essays show who you are through a specific story.
Show growth, reflection and voice.
Start with a vivid moment, not a dictionary definition.
lessons.try: Brainstorm ten moments that shaped you.

learn: Write freely first, then shape and cut.
Get feedback from trusted readers.
Proofread aloud; stay within word limits.
lessons.try: Draft a 650-word personal essay.

learn: A strong argument has a clear claim, evidence and reasoning.
Address counterarguments fairly.
Avoid fallacies: ad hominem, straw man, false dilemma.
check: Distorting an opponent's view is a...
lessons.try: Write an argument essay with a rebuttal.

learn: Begin with a focused, arguable question.
Use databases, libraries and scholarly sources.
Evaluate sources for authority, accuracy and bias.
lessons.try: Write a research question and find five credible sources.

learn: Organise notes by idea, not by source.
Use quotations, paraphrases and summaries with citations.
Your argument leads; sources support it.
lessons.try: Create an outline organised by idea.

learn: MLA and APA are common citation styles.
Plagiarism is presenting others' work as your own.
Using AI writing tools without permission or disclosure can break academic honesty rules.
check: Plagiarism means presenting others' work as...
lessons.try: Write a 2,000-word research paper with a Works Cited page.
